transcript.text:
The Anvil Father's people say the mountain is a forge and Greyhollow is its hearth. The town is cut into the cold flank of the peak, its houses and smithies stacked along a switchback road, and everything in it smells of coal smoke, iron dust, and snowmelt. Brakka Ironvein has kept the temple gate there for six years, an acolyte who learned to hold a sword as readily as a censer.

Three days ago three miners broke the seal on the old north workings and went down, and none came back. Last night a fourth man climbed out alone, raving about lights that walked, and died before dawn. At sunrise tomorrow the town council will brick the entrance shut again, and whatever is down there will be walled in with the dark.

Now the sun hangs low and cold behind the peaks. Brakka stands at the mine mouth, a borrowed temple lantern in one hand. The old timbers of the entrance lean like rotten teeth, and the chain that once barred the doors has been cut and hangs in a loop. Cold air pours up out of the dark, smelling of wet stone and old iron. Somewhere below, water drips.

What do you do?
